summary: This note outlines GreenHorizon Solutions' transportation and mileage reimbursement policy, with a focus on electric vehicles (EVs). It covers who is eligible, how reimbursement rates and EV charging costs are handled, record-keeping duties, and how the policy supports the company's sustainability goals. The policy is mandatory, reviewed annually, and expected to adapt as EV technology and costs change.
one_line: GreenHorizon Solutions' policy for reimbursing employee business mileage and EV charging costs, designed to support sustainability goals and adapt to the rise of electric vehicles.
key_facts: GreenHorizon Solutions' policy aims to ensure fair and equitable reimbursement for employees using personal vehicles for business while aligning with sustainability goals.
The policy applies to all full-time and part-time employees who travel for business and choose to use personal vehicles, including EVs, rather than company-provided transportation.
Traditional mileage reimbursement is based on Internal Revenue Service (IRS) standard mileage rates, which the company predicts may be adjusted to reflect the different cost of 'fueling' an EV.
GreenHorizon Solutions will adopt a formula for EV mileage reimbursement that accounts for energy costs per mile, maintenance, and depreciation specific to electric vehicles.
The EV formula is intended to ensure equity between EV drivers and internal combustion engine vehicle drivers.
Reimbursement rates will be adjusted yearly, or as needed, informed by industry standards, national averages for electricity rates, and EV-specific operating costs.
GreenHorizon Solutions will reimburse the actual cost of charging an EV for business travel, including public charging station fees.
Employees must submit charging receipts along with their mileage logs to receive charging reimbursement.
Employees using EVs must keep detailed logs of business travel miles and provide evidence of electricity costs; mobile apps or EV telematics solutions may be used for tracking and reporting.
The company foresees its fleet transitioning to electric models, and the policy creates incentives for employees to choose environmentally friendly transportation.
Compliance with the policy is mandatory for all employees.
The policy will be reviewed annually, with revisions reflecting changes in technology costs, environmental standards, and legislative imperatives regarding EVs.
The policy supersedes all previous travel and expense policies on transportation and mileage reimbursement; its effective date is left as a placeholder, '[insert effective date]'.
Employees with questions or suggestions about the policy are encouraged to contact the Human Resources department.
